record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Do cosmic microwave background anisotropy measurements and acoustic-peak fits provide robust predictions of the standard cosmological model, or are the fitted peaks and inferred parameters vulnerable to ad hoc refitting, foreground contamination from Galactic dust or other sources, and alternative interpretations such as quasi-steady-state cosmology or modified Newtonian dynamics?

evidence.quote: Apparently, the history of Microwave Background Radiation is a set of predictions which do not fit the observations but allow to modify the model to fit them ad hoc. This is called “successful predictions of the standard model”.

Apparently, these remarks were unfruitful since all the corrections of the galactic contamination continue to be carried out in the same wrong way: using templates and/or constant spectral index of the galactic dust contamination.

Nonetheless, subsequent observations, like those of Boomerang balloon-borne[164], have proven that, at least in some regions of low Galactic contamination, the microwave background radiation anisotropies over a larger range of frequencies is frequency independent, so something which is not dust should be producing these anisotropies, probably the same source which emits the average CMBR.

artifact.category_tag: CMB anisotropies and cosmological parameter estimation
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the angular power spectrum C_ℓ of temperature anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), measured as fluctuations ΔT/T on the sky and decomposed in spherical harmonics so that C_ℓ = ⟨|a_{ℓm}|²⟩. In the standard ΛCDM cosmological model, the locations, heights, and relative spacings of the acoustic peaks in C_ℓ are predicted as functions of cosmological parameters (baryon density Ω_b h², matter density Ω_m h², curvature Ω_k, dark energy density Ω_Λ, scalar spectral index n_s, optical depth τ, and amplitude A_s) via linear perturbation theory of a photon–baryon fluid coupled to dark matter and gravity.

Address the following:

(a) Quantify the robustness of cosmological-parameter inference from acoustic-peak fitting under the following perturbations of the analysis pipeline:
  (i) systematic re-fitting that allows additional nuisance parameters or priors after first-look comparisons with data;
  (ii) Galactic foreground subtraction performed with template-based methods assuming a spatially constant spectral index for thermal dust emission, versus methods allowing spatial variation of the dust spectral index;
  (iii) the presence of an unmodeled anisotropy component whose frequency spectrum coincides with that of the CMB blackbody itself (and is therefore not separable from the CMB by multi-frequency component separation).

(b) Determine whether, under (i)–(iii), the standard-model best-fit parameters {Ω_b h², Ω_m h², Ω_Λ, n_s, …} are uniquely determined to within their quoted statistical errors, or whether alternative cosmological frameworks — specifically a quasi-steady-state cosmology (with a creation field producing iron-whisker thermalization of starlight as a CMB origin) and Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND, replacing cold dark matter by a modification a → μ(a/a_0) a of the gravitational acceleration law at a_0 ≈ 1.2 × 10^{−10} m/s²) — can produce a comparable fit to the observed peak structure with statistically indistinguishable goodness-of-fit.

Provide either a rigorous demonstration that the standard ΛCDM parameter inference from CMB acoustic peaks is robust against (i)–(iii) and uniquely preferred over the listed alternatives, or explicit counterexamples showing that it is not.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad methodological/foundational critique rather than a precise mathematical conjecture. Mainstream CMB analyses (WMAP, Planck) report that ΛCDM remains an excellent fit to acoustic-peak data with stable parameter inference, while a minority literature continues to argue that foreground modeling and alternative cosmologies (QSSC, MOND-based) deserve more scrutiny. No definitive resolution of the broad claim exists; status is best described as unknown/ongoing debate.

status_evidence.title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters
status_evidence.snippet: The base-ΛCDM model continues to provide an excellent fit to the CMB data.
status_evidence.claim: Mainstream analyses report ΛCDM robustly fits CMB acoustic peaks.
